findings.title: Illustrative heading structure
findings.summary: A hypothetical page starts with a level-one heading, then skips to a level-three heading.
findings.meaning: Heading levels can help people scan a page and move through it with assistive technology. A skipped level is a prompt to review the structure, not proof that a page is unusable.
findings.verification: Inspect the rendered heading outline or browser accessibility tree, then confirm the headings describe the page's sections.
findings.owner: Website owner or content editor, with implementation support if needed
findings.recheck: No recheck is available. This is a static example; no website was scanned.

findings.title: Illustrative image text alternative question
findings.summary: A hypothetical informative image has no accessible text alternative.
findings.meaning: People who do not see the image may miss its purpose. Decorative images can use an empty alternative so they do not add noise.
findings.verification: Inspect the image's accessible name in the browser accessibility tree and decide whether the image is informative or decorative in context.
findings.before: Example before: informative image with no accessible name
findings.after: Illustrative update: a concise alternative, or an empty alternative if decorative
findings.recheck: No recheck is available. This is a static example; no website was scanned.
